# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 37 (Bu-Vb Sk37)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk37
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 37
**Title (English, from literature):** Requesting rice and bean curry

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sūpodanaviññatti-sikkhāpada* ("Requesting rice and bean curry") is the thirty-seventh training rule in the *Sekhiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Vin IV 193,30–31) [Hüsken 1997]. The rule prohibits monastics who are not sick (*agilāna*) from soliciting cooked rice and curry (*sūpodana*) for their own consumption, establishing that doing so incurs an offense of wrong conduct (*dukkaṭa*) [Hüsken 1997]. In the commentary (*Samantapāsādikā*), this training rule is referenced in discussions of food-solicitation casuistry to distinguish the general *sekhiya* offense for requesting staple curry and rice from the more severe offenses governing requests for exquisite or rich foods (*panītabhojana*) [Hüsken 1997].

 It appears in the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Sekhiya 37), both Pātimokkhas, and the *Parivāra*, as well as in the monastic codes of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions preserved in Chinese and Sanskrit. DharmaNexus detects extensive internal Vinaya text reuse, matching formulaic phraseology across numerous rules concerning food and conduct, notably with *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* Pācittiya 39, Pācittiya 32, and Pācittiya 57, and cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation of the rule has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
